records.move: Banco Central del Ecuador (Delegado-Vocal de la Junta Monetaria, 1981) to Banco de la Produccion S.A. Produbanco (Director Alterno, member of the board, 2014 to present)
records.summary: Produbanco's own website publishes the CV of board member Juan Diego Mosquera Pesantes. It lists, for 1981, "Banco Central del Ecuador. Delegado-Vocal de la Junta Monetaria", and from 2014 to the present "Banco de la Produccion S.A. Produbanco. Director Alterno, Miembro del directorio". Produbanco's ownership is stated by the bank itself in its 2023 corporate report, which says "Produbanco continua siendo el unico banco de capital privado en Latinoamerica que cuenta con la certificacion de Empresa B" - that is, a bank of private capital. Produbanco's head office city is not stated in the pages read, so it is left blank.

records.move: Banco de Cochabamba S.A. (senior position, no date given) to Banco Central de Bolivia (Gerente de Operaciones Internacionales 1994-1996, Gerente General 1996-2006 and again from 16 January 2020)
records.summary: The Banco Central de Bolivia publishes the CV of its General Manager Jaime Valencia Valencia. It says he was General Manager of the central bank from 1996 to 2006 and again from 16 January 2020, and that he "Ocupo cargos importantes en" a list of firms that includes "Banco de Cochabamba S.A." The CV gives no dates or titles for that bank. Ownership of the Banco de Cochabamba is stated by the US Library of Congress Bolivia country study, which places the "Bank of Cochabamba" among the country's top five commercial banks holding 61 percent of deposits at the end of 1988, says "commercial banks remained the core of the private financial sector", and separately lists the public-sector institutions as "the Central Bank, BAB, Bamin, and the State Bank (Banco del Estado--Banest)", which does not include it. No source read states the bank's head office city, so it is left blank.
records.source_title: Jaime Valencia Valencia - Gerente General, Banco Central de Bolivia (CV published by the BCB)
records.quote: Fue Gerente General titular e institucionalizado del Banco Central de Bolivia de 1996 a 2006, tambien se desempeno como Gerente de Operaciones Internacionales del BCB de 1994 a 1996. Ocupo cargos importantes en: Grupo Empresarial Monterrey; Ferrocarril Nuevo Central Argentino; Ingenio Sucroalcoholero Aguai; Jindal Steel Bolivia S.A.; Ferroviaria Oriental S.A.; Banco de la Union S.A.; Banco de Cochabamba; Compania Boliviana de Seguros S.A.; Comision Nacional de Estudio de la Cana y del Azucar

records.move: Governor and Chairman of the Board of the Central Bank of Sudan (1973-1980) to General Manager of the National Bank (1980-1982)
records.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan's own page for former governor Ibrahim Mohammed Ali Nimir lists his work experience as "General Manager, National Bank, 1980 - 1982" directly after "Governor and Chairman Board of Directors, Central Bank of Sudan, 1973 - 1980". The National Bank of Sudan states its own ownership on its website: "The National Bank of Sudan was established in 1981 as an initiative by a group of national Sudanese businessmen", and the bank remained in Sudanese private hands until July 2006, when "75% of the value of the NBS shares were acquired by the Lebanese Bank Audi". The bank's own founding year of 1981 falls inside the 1980-1982 term the central bank gives for Nimir. No source read states a head office city, so it is left blank.

held.missing: No source read states who owned Compania Boliviana de Seguros S.A. The 1946 founding capital split is not an ownership statement for the years the official worked there, and the Los Tiempos anniversary piece on its successor La Boliviana Ciacruz names no shareholders. Not needed for the Bolivian record above, which is settled on the Banco de Cochabamba, but still open if the insurer is to be counted separately.

No source read states who owned the Workers National Bank in 1989-1992. Sudanese bank name registers and a Dabanga news item mention the bank but say nothing about its shareholders; whether it was a state, trade-union or privately held bank in those years is unstated. Not needed for the Sudan record above, which is settled on the 1980-1982 move to the National Bank.
